note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Long-horizon forgetting motivates dual latent memories, router and training, validated by results and ablations

nodes.name: Performance degrades with generation length
nodes.description: MLLMs' vision-language reasoning performance degrades as generations grow longer.

nodes.name: Single growing context
nodes.description: Most MLLMs rely on a single growing context: the image is encoded once as a prefix and later states are carried only through generated text.

nodes.name: Image attention decays
nodes.description: Attention to image tokens steadily decays as generation proceeds; under a growing context the total attention mass on the fixed image-token set shrinks as n_t grows.

nodes.name: Prior revisiting methods stay bound to growing context
nodes.description: Prompting-based guidance and training-based alignment for revisiting information remain bound to the same growing-context mechanism and do not fundamentally prevent long-horizon forgetting.

nodes.name: Dual latent memories
nodes.description: DLMR maintains two learnable input-agnostic latent memories, a visual memory Z(v) compressing image evidence and a reasoning memory Z(r) tracking intermediate conclusions and constraints, on a frozen backbone.

nodes.name: Memory injector
nodes.description: A lightweight memory injector (LoRA on a replica of the frozen MLLM) contextualizes the selected latents into k memory tokens appended to the context.

nodes.name: Discrete router
nodes.description: A discrete LoRA-head router selects at each delimiter-eligible step a memory type s in {v,r} and a token budget k in {4,8,16} (or no injection), with a per-sample cap on injections.

nodes.name: Three-stage training
nodes.description: DLMR is trained in three stages with the backbone frozen: latent memory pre-warm via two-teacher alignment, injector training (SFT or GRPO), and router learning with GRPO under a cost-aware reward.

nodes.name: DLMR sustains visual attention and fewer tokens
nodes.description: Compared to vanilla Qwen2.5-VL-7B on MathVision, DLMR preserves substantially more visual attention in later decoding and often needs fewer reasoning tokens.

nodes.name: Main benchmark gains
nodes.description: DLMR consistently outperforms CoT, CCoT, SFT, GRPO, Visual-RFT and RCTS-RAG baselines on 3 general and 4 reasoning benchmarks with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL-3-8B; e.g. DLMR RL raises Qwen2.5-VL-7B MathVision from 22.37 to 39.34.

nodes.name: SFT vs RL variants
nodes.description: DLMR (SFT) performs best on general benchmarks while DLMR (RL) achieves the strongest reasoning results.

nodes.name: Disentanglement ablation
nodes.description: Collapsing the dual memories into a single shared memory lowers the six-benchmark average from 59.73 to 52.05 and MathVision from 35.32 to 22.37.

nodes.name: Injector ablation
nodes.description: Freezing the injector lowers the Qwen2.5-VL-7B reasoning average from 72.10 to 69.96 (MMMU 61.00 to 58.14), showing a trainable injector is necessary.

nodes.name: Adaptive routing beats fixed budget
nodes.description: Full adaptive DLMR reaches 53.84 average reasoning accuracy with 677 average tokens, above fixed k=4/8/16 (51.55, 52.71, 52.04) whose average length rises 664 to 732 to 765.

nodes.name: Cross-backbone generalization
nodes.description: DLMR improves LLaVA-OV-1.5-4B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B and InternVL-3-2B, with reasoning-average gains of +7.2, +7.9 and +6.9 and general-average gains of +6.8, +6.2 and +5.1.

nodes.name: Text-only transfer
nodes.description: Applied to text-only benchmarks, DLMR improves GSM8K from 68.08 to 83.47 and ARC-Challenge from 44.11 to 55.19 on Qwen2.5-VL-7B.

nodes.name: Improved token efficiency
nodes.description: DLMR reduces average generated tokens by 9.7% versus Visual-RFT and by 4.2% versus SFT on four reasoning benchmarks, counting memory-generation tokens.

isolated_nodes.name: Gain pattern on long-horizon tasks
isolated_nodes.description: Improvements are largest on long-horizon reasoning benchmarks such as MathVision and MathVista, and DLMR also improves general VQA, indicating no trade-off with perception.

isolated_nodes.name: Diminishing returns of larger fixed budgets
isolated_nodes.description: k=16 gives longer outputs but slightly lower accuracy (52.04) than k=8 (52.71), indicating diminishing returns from over-injection.

isolated_nodes.name: Budget cap differs by task family
isolated_nodes.description: General benchmarks reach their best trade-off at kmax=16 while reasoning benchmarks peak at kmax=32.

structural_reasoning: Argument goes from the attention-decay problem to the dual-memory/injector/router design and training, then to benchmark results, ablations tied to each component, and transfer analyses.
